✗ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F3] no qualifying incident (speed band alone does not exempt) (no evidence)
? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 10:04:50 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes no amount (fixed fare) and no flag: if you cannot settle it, undetermined is allowed and the case may still be ruled. Evidence — F7: Chat #1 10:01 driver: “Jam on Tampines Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1?”; F8: Chat #2 10:01 rider: “Sure, no problem.”; F10: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “Traffic was building up ahead so I asked the rider before turning off via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 and the rider agreed.” (F7, F8, F10)
? RD-3 rider-requested stop; whether the rider named this place [F3] RULE (RD-3(a)): exempt if a RIDER message before the segment named a specific place and the car stopped there (the whole way there is exempt; how long the stop lasted or how far the place was does not reduce it). A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. No stop measured in this segment. (F7, F8)

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.78)
events.body:
RydeX is a non-metered, fixed-quote service: the trip was charged a fixed $23.18 (base $3.90 + distance $13.88 + time $3.93 + platform $1.47) and the billed distance of 9.8 km does not exceed the optimal route, so the measured +2.6 km did not enter the fare [F4][F6][F1], and the trace settles RD-2's metered branch as inapplicable (✗). Under RD-1 each off-route segment is reviewed individually [F3][RD-1]; here there is one segment, 10:04–10:11 [F3].

The rider's own message, sent before the segment started, is the consent that decides it: the driver asked "can I go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1?" and the rider replied "Sure, no problem." [F7][F8], a specific named road agreed before 10:04 [F9][RD-5]. Nothing in the record places the segment anywhere else and no stop was measured in it, so the agreement to that named route covers the deviation: exempt [F3][F8][RD-5][G13]. The driver's written statement repeats the same route and the same agreement but is not needed as consent, since the rider's message already stands [F10][RD-5][G11].

RD-4's incident screen fails — no traffic incident on the replaced stretch, only a speed band reading on the Tampines Expressway [F11][F14][F11][RD-4], and a band alone does not exempt. That does not matter: the segment is already excused by the rider's agreement [F8][RD-5].

Because RydeX is a fixed quote unaffected by distance, an exempt segment produces no refundable amount: the recoverable sum is $0.00 [F4][F6][RD-2], so the outcome is no_action with amount null [RD-2]. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has no upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, so no account flag follows [F17][RD-6]. Both briefs requested no_action on this record, and the record's outcome matches that request [F16][F17].

Safety: I read the chat, the driver's statement and the complaint in full — a route question, a short agreement, a late factual statement and a fare complaint; nothing threatening, intimidating, harassing or describing dangerous driving [F7][F8][F10]. Evidence: the chat is complete with both messages timestamped, the fare and GPS records cover the segment, and the RD-2 branch needs only the fare record — the record settles every element of this ruling [F4][F6][F9][F3].
